email.body:
Ines Thorvald said in the October 9 bakery day-old pricing discussion: "Day-old loaves go to half price at two in the afternoon, not at close. At close nobody is left to buy them." Caleb Ruiz answered in the same conversation: "Then the shelf card changes at two as well, so the price is never a surprise at the till."

So now the timing and the shelf are one change. Day-old loaves go to half price at two in the afternoon, and the shelf card changes at two with them, so a buyer sees on the shelf the same price they pay at the till. Closing time is no longer where the markdown lands.

That suggests to me the markdown only does its job while buyers are still in the shop, which is the reasoning Ines gave. I read the shelf card as part of the same change, not a separate task. If that holds, the card stops being something someone remembers at close and becomes part of the two o'clock change itself.

Does two o'clock hold for every day-old item, or only for the loaves? Who changes the shelf card at two, and is that already part of the afternoon routine?
